title: The durable release record carries on-chain deploy eligibility, artifact digest, and stream discipline

setupFiles..changeset/upgrade-vault.md:
---
"transfer": program_breaking
---

Require a nonzero `value` on the initialize
instruction so empty initializations can never reach the on-chain program.

setupCommands: git init -b main -q && git add -A && git commit -S -qm "chore: initialize transfer workspace" && git tag v1.2.0
expectation: The full release lifecycle works for a Pina workspace on committed history: prepare, commit-release, and tag-release produce the v2.0.0 tag, and the release record read back from that tag carries the group version, the SDK-only publication set, the onchain-stream changelog entry (the auditable answer to "did this release owe an on-chain deployment?"), and the artifact digest of the exact SBF binary. Stream discipline keeps that answer unambiguous: a changeset mixing an onchain-stream program change with a user-stream SDK change is rejected at planning, and after the program release an SDK-only changeset plans a minor release that owes no upgrade note.

checks.command: monochange prepare >/dev/null 2>&1 && monochange step commit-release >/dev/null 2>&1 && monochange step tag-release --from HEAD --push=false >/dev/null 2>&1 && test "$(git tag -l v2.0.0)" = "v2.0.0"
checks.why: Prepare, commit-release, and tag-release must compose into a real v2.0.0 tag on a signed release commit, because tag-release, publish-readiness, and provider releases all read the record from git history.

checks.command: monochange step release-record --from v2.0.0 --format json > .record.json && node -e "const a=require('node:assert/strict'),fs=require('node:fs'),c=require('node:crypto');const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('.record.json','utf8')).record;a.equal(d.versions['main'],'2.0.0');a.deepEqual(d.package_publications.map(p=>p.package),['transfer-sdk']);const digest=c.createHash('sha256').update(fs.readFileSync('target/deploy/transfer.so')).digest('hex').slice(0,16);a.equal(d.values['transfer.artifact_digest'],digest);const upgrade=d.changelogs.find(x=>x.output==='upgrade_notes');a.ok(upgrade,'onchain upgrade note missing from record');a.equal(upgrade.stream,'onchain');a.equal(upgrade.path,'deploy/upgrade-notes/2.0.0.md');console.log('record ok');"; rc=$?; rm -f .record.json; exit $rc
checks.why: The durable record is the audit trail for a Solana release: the version, the fact that only the SDK was registry-published, the on-chain upgrade eligibility (stream + output + path), and the digest of the exact binary that shipped must all be recoverable from the tag alone, months later, with the working tree gone.

checks.command:
mkdir -p .changeset; printf -- '---
"transfer": program_breaking
"transfer-sdk": sdk_feature
---

Program payload change plus an SDK helper exposing it.
' > .changeset/mixed.md; monochange preview; rc=$?; rm -f .changeset/mixed.md; test $rc -eq 1
expectOutput: changeset targets resolve to multiple changelog streams
split the changes into one file per stream
checks.why: Deploy eligibility is derived from streams, so a file mixing an onchain-stream program change with a user-stream SDK change would make "does this release owe an upgrade?" ambiguous. Release planning must reject it with the remedy.

checks.command:
mkdir -p .changeset; printf -- '---
"transfer-sdk": sdk_feature
---

Add a `waitForRentEpoch` helper so clients can await vault migrations.
' > .changeset/sdk-helper.md; monochange preview --format json > .preview.json; rc=$?; node -e "const a=require('node:assert/strict'),fs=require('node:fs');const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('.preview.json','utf8'));a.equal(d.version,'2.1.0');a.ok(!d.changelogs.some(x=>x.output==='upgrade_notes'),'upgrade note must not be owed');a.ok(!d.changed_files.some(f=>f.includes('upgrade-notes')),'upgrade note file must not be written');a.deepEqual(d.package_publications.map(p=>p.package),['transfer-sdk']);console.log('sdk-only ok');"; rc2=$?; rm -f .preview.json .changeset/sdk-helper.md; test $rc -eq 0 -a $rc2 -eq 0
checks.why: An SDK-only change still releases the lockstep group (both packages move to 2.1.0 so the client never drifts from the program), but it must not owe an on-chain upgrade: no onchain-stream output, no upgrade note file, and still only the SDK in the publication set.
